A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed a CMOS differential amplifier that can operate at a high bandwidth and low noise level.
the design and fabrication of a CMOS differential amplifier with a transimpedence of 1.27 M Omega, a noise current of 4.5 picoA/spl radic/(Hz) and a bandwidth of 60 MHz has been completed.
a high speed, low noise CMOS transimpedance amplifier channel for the receiver of laser range finding devices has been designed and fabricated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a differential amplifier channel can reduce the input-referred noise by more than 50% and the input-referred offset voltage by more than 90% compared to a single-ended channel.
a high performance differential amplifier channel can be designed using a standard CMOS process with a low cost and a high yield.
